c: The global argument over artificial
intelligence has reached a moment of
extraordinary confusion. Some of the
people building the most powerful AI
systems are warning that the technology
could become uncontrollable, destroy
millions of jobs, supercharge biological
and cyber warfare, and perhaps even
threaten human survival. Others,
including most recently the Nvidia
chief, Jensen Huang, dismisses the
extinction warnings as unscientific
fear-mongering and insist there is
virtually no chance of AI destroying
humanity. Governments are caught between
two imperatives now. Control a
technology its own creators say may be
dangerous,
and accelerate it before a strategic
rival, particularly China, gets there
first.
Meanwhile, the systems themselves are
becoming more capable, more autonomous,
and increasingly difficult even for
their creators to fully understand.
So, is this a genuine emergency,
exaggerated apocalyptic marketing, or a
warning arriving just before humanity
crosses a point of no return?
Few people are better qualified to
answer that question than my guest
tonight.
He has spent decades championing neural
networks when much of computer science
dismissed them. His work helped lay the
foundations for modern deep learning.
He later left Google after a decade so
he could speak freely about the dangers
of artificial intelligence. He is a
Turing Award winner, a Nobel laureate,
and the man the world knows as one of
the godfathers of AI. Professor Geoffrey
Hinton, it's a privilege to have you.
Welcome.
>> Thank you for inviting me.
>> Professor Hinton, my first question,
Jensen Huang of Nvidia says there is a
0% chance, in his words,
that AI will destroy humanity. You've

There's a significant risk. Nobody can

feelings.

interests.
>> So, are you saying that this is
apocalypse marketing? This is in the
interests of the companies that are
issuing these warnings.
>> Not at all. No. The people in the
companies issuing these warnings make
sacrifices to do that.
Um one of the CEOs, Dario Amodei, made a
sacrifice by issuing this warning before
his comp- company goes public.
Um the people who are saying there's no
chance at all of it causing any damage,
like Jensen Huang, have a large

Why isn't there more of a pushback in

critics say extinction warnings are

And
they are capable now of creating new

can hire
capacity from
providers on the web like Amazon.

>> So, we're at a point where rogue agents

if you're in control of a classroom full
full of two year olds, how many ways

where
things need to be either paused or

>> I think we just reached that point. The
point where agents are powerful enough

Agents are powerful enough that they can

communication
between agents.
>> Yes.

large-scale
damage to accounts of any kind? That's

populists.
Um
we will

Um obviously, if you don't like people

It it's famously called the but what

>> And if the Chinese Communist Party
